enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 18–30 regulate the partner’s agency relationship with the firm, implied authority, emergency authority, restrictions on authority, liability of the firm for partner acts, holding out, transfer of a partner’s interest and the special statutory position of minors admitted to the benefits of partnership.

Definition: A partner is the agent of the firm for the purposes of the business of the firm, and the Act allocates authority and third-party liability accordingly.

Ingredients:
1. Identify the firm and partner acting as agent.
2. Determine whether the act is within the ordinary course or implied authority.
3. Apply statutory restrictions and emergency rules.
4. Test firm liability for partner acts and holding out.
5. For minors, apply section 30 separately to benefits and liabilities.
examples: A partner purchases ordinary stock for the firm in the usual course of its business; the act is tested as an act of the firm under the partner-agency provisions.
problemApplication: Apply sections 18–30: identify the statutory relationship or transaction, test each ingredient, consider exceptions or limitations, and conclude.
keyTakeaways: Sections 18–30 regulate the partner’s agency relationship with the firm, implied authority, emergency authority, restrictions on authority, liability of the firm for partner acts, holding out, transfer of a partner’s interest and the special statutory position of minors admitted to the benefits of partnership.
